biteOfDay: Bass on Table Rock have settled into fall patterns, holding on long points, gravel flats that drop into deeper water, and offshore structure as they feed ahead of winter. Walleye and crappie continue producing around brush piles and points. On Taneycomo, stocked rainbows stay active while brown trout activity increases with the cooler water. tableRock.clarity: Gin-clear near dam; verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.
taneycomo.generation: ~3,486 cfs at 10:00 CT (USACE live). Overnight ~20; afternoon peak ~3,486. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Insider tip: During early low-flow windows on Taneycomo (always confirm the current SWPA schedule at 866-494-1993), drift or wade the seams and current breaks with light 2-lb test and a 1/16- to 1/8-oz marabou micro jig in black, sculpin, or olive (often with an orange head) or a #18-20 zebra midge
